messages.subject: Work Group Tomorrow: 10-noon
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

As a reminder, we will have our weekly work group tomorrow from 10-noon. With the UC Davis transition to in-person classes, we will now be hosting hybrid-style D-RUG working groups, so you can join either remotely or in-person. If you join remotely, please remember to post questions on our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site ahead of time. More info below.

Best,
Christian

________________________________________________________________
This quarter we'll be meeting from 10-noon on Wednesdays (same as last fall). In light of the recent move to in-person classes, we will be meeting in a hybrid format, via zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>, and in the Data Lab classroom (360 Shields Library).

Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. In the past, we've had (15- to 45-minute) presentations ranging from data types, to tidyverse tools, to spatial data, to the Google Earth Engine plugin for R. If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar <https://d-rug.github.io/calendar.html>! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).

--
Christian John — Ph.D. candidate
NASA FINESST Future Investigator
Pronouns: he/him/his

Google Scholar <https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=VPd60tMAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&authuser=1&sortby=pubdate>
